claims.text: A controlled dwell at a critical nucleation temperature enhances atomic diffusion and homogenization of noble-metal precursors.
The dwell produces simultaneous nucleation under near-equilibrium conditions.
Simultaneous nucleation promoted by the dwell favors a uniform single-phase FCC structure.
Before thermal processing, the noble-metal precursor compounds are well mixed, supported, and in a solid precursor state.
The proposed process uses a dwell lasting tens of seconds to minutes at a temperature just below the rapid thermal-decomposition threshold, followed by rapid cooling.
An optimized dwell provides enough atomic mobility for homogenization without causing coarsening or unwanted phase transitions.
The dwell reduces differential diffusion among the constituent noble metals.
Reduced differential diffusion enables synchronized nucleation.
Synchronized nucleation minimizes stochastic elemental segregation and suppresses phase separation.
Rapid cooling can kinetically retain a single high-entropy solid-solution state by suppressing secondary-phase formation.
Relative to rapid heating and cooling without a dwell, the intervention will increase single-phase FCC uniformity.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will reduce elemental segregation and phase separation.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will improve morphology control and lattice-parameter consistency.
Rapid heat-cool processing without a dwell often causes uncontrolled nucleation, phase separation, elemental segregation, and variable particle morphology.
Rapid high-temperature processing can decompose supported mixed-metal precursors and then crystallize the resulting material during rapid cooling.
The proposed dwell mechanism applies only near the precursor-decomposition threshold and within noble-metal compositions capable of forming an FCC lattice.
Excessively long dwell times or temperature deviations can cause coarsening or phase changes.
The optimal dwell time and temperature window depend on precursor composition and support material.
